MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:44 AM
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. articles.title: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech
articles.snippet: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech Hoodline
articles.text:
555 12th St. — Oakland Street Scene
Google Street View
An Oakland health-tech company has raised $140 million in a new funding round. Vumedi, which builds an AI-powered learning platform for physicians, has raised $140 million in Series B funding, with plans to pour the money into talent, research and development, product development and outreach as it expands its clinical learning tools.
The investment came from Oak HC/FT, according to FinSMEs , which reported the round. Vumedi is led by founder and CEO Roman Giverts, and the company describes its platform as a tool that connects clinicians with specialists and peers so they can learn procedures, evaluate treatments and navigate complex cases, the outlet reports.
What the Platform Actually Does
At the center of Vumedi's pitch is scale paired with AI. The platform uses artificial intelligence to turn more than 100,000 physician-led videos and nearly 5,000 podcast episodes, spanning more than 21 medical specialties, into what the company calls an on-demand clinical resource, per the same report. Rather than leaving clinicians to sift through hours of footage, the system synthesizes multiple expert perspectives and links directly to time-stamped segments within videos.
The company says its platform now serves more than 150,000 NPI-verified clinicians and generated over 56 million minutes of learning over the past 12 months. Back in a 2018 interview, Giverts described Vumedi's mission as helping physicians make the best care decisions through what he called unbiased video education in an interview with MPO-mag.com . That same article reported the platform then had roughly 250,000 physician users and 20,000 videos contributed by more than 5,000 healthcare organizations and professionals, including partnerships with 150 hospitals and conferences such as Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic and Johns Hopkins.
Funding Figures Don't All Line Up
Not every account of Vumedi's fundraising history tells the same story. A snippet from 01net referenced a $104 million investment from Oak HC/FT, though it's unclear from that report whether it describes the same financing as the newly reported $140 million round or a separate transaction. Separately, CB Insights lists Vumedi's most recent funding round as a $79.98 million Series B dated May 22, 2025, and puts the company's total raised at $82.08 million across four rounds. The available reporting does not reconcile these differing figures with the $140 million sum reported this week.
Part of a Broader AI Health-Tech Wave
Vumedi's raise lands amid a broader uptick in digital-health investment. Companies in the sector raised $7.4 billion in the first half of 2026, up roughly $1 billion from the same period in 2025, according to Fierce Healthcare . The outlet counted 244 completed deals in that window, with $4.2 billion invested in the first quarter and $3.2 billion in the second.
A notable share of that capital came in the form of megadeals. Nineteen companies raised 20 financings of at least $100 million in the first half of 2026, representing 45 percent of all capital invested, Fierce Healthcare reported, citing deals that included AI radiology company Aidoc's $150 million raise. Clinical-reference platform OpenEvidence, a comparable player in physician-facing AI tools, announced its own $210 million Series B at a $3.5 billion valuation in mid-2025, co-led by Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins with Sequoia Capital, Coatue, Conviction and Thrive also participa

articles.title: Co-Brand Card Platform Imprint Raises $130M at a $1.9B Valuation as AI Reshapes Commerce
articles.snippet: Co-Brand Card Platform Imprint Raises $130M at a $1.9B Valuation as AI Reshapes Commerce Wowtale
articles.text:
When AI shopping assistants find, compare and pay for products, brands risk losing their direct relationship with customers. McKinsey projects that agentic commerce could mediate up to $1 trillion in U.S. retail revenue by 2030. Imprint , which builds co-branded credit cards so brands can stay part of everyday spending, has raised $130 million.
Co-branded cards, built from the ground up
Imprint is a payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform that helps brands make every transaction more valuable. Founded in 2020 and based in New York, it builds co-branded credit cards with brands and owns its stack across origination, risk, servicing and rewards. That gives brands control of their financial products and room to tailor rewards, the company says.
Since the start of the year it has launched programs with Albertsons Companies, Fanatics, Kroger and Shell, with the Fanatics card debuting this week. Booking.com is also a customer. Imprint reports more than two million members and partners whose annual U.S. consumer spending exceeds $500 billion. Total cardholder spending across its partners more than doubled between 2025 and 2026, and the share of spending on Imprint cards at partner checkouts tripled in a year. It also added $1.5 billion in warehouse capacity and priced its second AAA-rated asset-backed securitization, with demand nearly five times the offering size. These figures come from the company.
For the AI era, Imprint released a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents securely reach members’ rewards, virtual cards and transaction history, along with tools for members to review and authorize agent-initiated purchases. Imprint Access, launching today, gives customers who are new to credit or rebuilding it, backed by a refundable deposit, the same ongoing rewards as a brand’s unsecured card, with a path to upgrade. The Federal Reserve estimates 32 million Americans have little or no credit history.
A law graduate from Dublin who came to cards through WeWork
Founder and CEO Daragh Murphy is Irish, studied law at University College Dublin and was a vice president of operations and strategy at WeWork, according to Irish media. He founded Imprint in 2020 with Gaurav Ahuja and Michael Pechman. Ahuja, a partner at Thrive Capital , is reported to have helped incubate the company and to serve as chairman. Imprint raised a $75 million Series C at a $600 million valuation in October 2024, and press reports put its December 2025 Series D at $150 million and a $1.2 billion valuation.
Valuation up from $1.2B
Imprint said it raised $130 million at a valuation of about $1.9 billion. Existing investor Khosla Ventures led. Existing investors Hedosophia , Ribbit Capital , Spice and Thrive Capital took part, and Positive Sum joined as a new investor. The money will fund new payment options and AI capabilities, so brands can recognize and reward customers however they choose to pay. The release did not name the round.
CEO Murphy said brands that invest in understanding each customer and building individual relationships will win as every digital touchpoint becomes personalized. Patrick O’Shaughnessy, CEO and partner at Positive Sum, said AI makes every option easier to compare, so earning a customer’s preference matters more, and that the team’s full-stack technology and marquee partners gave the firm conviction. Fanatics CFO Glenn Schiffman said Imprint’s technology made it possible to design a card around fans.

Clara Raises $105 Million to Grow Latin American Corporate Spend Management Platform
By Julie Muhn (@julieschicktanz) Posted on November 13, 2026
Categories: Daily news , Funding
Clara raised $105 million, comprising a $65 million Series C equity round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility, bringing its total debt and equity funding to $838 million.
Clara will use the funding to expand its market reach and enhance its AI capabilities, including its MCP integration that enables AI agents to access financial data and execute authorized transactions.
The funding comes amid global growth in corporate card and spend management platforms, as providers expand beyond payments and expense tracking to offer integrated, AI-powered financial management tools.
Brazil-based spend management platform Clara raised $105 million this week. The round is comprised of $65 million in equity in a Series C round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF).
The $65 million Series C was anchored by Citius, Kaszek, and DEG, a subsidiary of Germany’s KfW Group. The round also attracted participation from 10 existing investors and three new investors, including CMT Digital and Nascent VC.
The latest investment brings Clara’s total debt and equity funding to $838 million, following several debt financing deals over the past year. In November 2025, Clara secured $70 million in structured debt financing from BBVA Spark, Covalto, and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). Three months later, the company renewed a $150 million credit facility with Goldman Sachs, bringing its total debt capacity to more than $250 million.
Clara will use today’s funding to expand its go-to-market team and strengthen the automation and AI capabilities of its platform. Clara was founded in 2020 and now helps more than 45,000 businesses automate routine work, control spending, and make better financial decisions. The company’s platform offers corporate cards, bill payments, spend management, accounts payable, and accounts receivable to help businesses make and manage payments. Along with the financing announcement, Clara said it has also surpassed $100 million in annualized net revenue and maintained positive EBITDA for more than a year.
Among Clara’s capabilities is its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration, which connects the platform with AI agents to enable customers to access real-time spending reports and forecasts using natural language, as well as execute authorized transactions autonomously. The company also offers AI-powered policy enforcement that checks employee expenses against company policies in real time, global spend management tools that allow businesses to manage expenses across countries and currencies, and fleet management solutions that support fuel payments and vehicle operations.
“Clara exists to champion Latin American businesses, and we work tirelessly to give them the tools to compete and win on the global stage,” said Clara Co-Founder and CEO Gerry Giacomán Colyer. “The region has long been underserved by financial platforms designed for other markets. We’re combining AI with local expertise to solve challenges specific to doing business here and give our customers a distinct competitive edge.”

articles.text:
Databento Raises $100 Million Series C at $1.1 Billion Valuation
News provided by
Databento Inc.
Nov 12, 2026, 08:57 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SALT LAKE CITY , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Databento, the market data platform for modern finance, today announced a $100 million Series C financing at a $1.1 billion valuation. The round was led by Fifth Down Capital, an early investor in Databento, with participation from nearly all of the company's existing investors, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital, and Hedosophia.
The announcement follows Databento's $97 million Series B earlier this year. Since closing its previous round, the company has more than doubled its revenue while remaining profitable.
Databento serves leading quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities firms, and digital asset companies. The company has also established a strong presence in artificial intelligence, having signed enterprise contracts with five of the six leading frontier AI labs.
Databento had 39 employees when it closed its Series C, reaching a $1.1 billion valuation with a fraction of the headcount of traditional market data providers.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry," said Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO of Databento. "Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow."
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data," said Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital. "Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing."
The round also included a strategic investment from Fitch Ventures, bringing the perspective of a leading financial information provider with deep expertise in credit ratings, financial data, and market insights.
"Financial data is becoming increasingly API-driven and machine-consumed, creating an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how institutions and other market participants access it," said Gabby Munoz, Global Head of M&A and Venture Investments at Fitch Group. "Databento has built differentiated infrastructure at the source and paired it with a modern, self-service model that makes institutional-grade market data available on demand. We're excited to back the team as they scale a platform we believe will help shape how market data is captured, delivered, and consumed."
The new funding will support Databento's continued investment in its market data infrastructure and expansion into additional asset classes.

articles.title: Rox Raises $100M at $1.3B Valuation as Aramco-Backed Prosperity7 Bets on AI Revenue Agents
articles.snippet: Rox Raises $100M at $1.3B Valuation as Aramco-Backed Prosperity7 Bets on AI Revenue Agents entARABI
articles.text:
Rox Raises $100M at $1.3B Valuation as Aramco-Backed Prosperity7 Bets on AI Revenue Agents
Published on: 13 November، 2026
Rox
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation,
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, with participation from Prosperity7 Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco.
The round was co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory participating alongside new investors, including Databricks Ventures.
From Customer Data to AI-Powered Sales Execution
Rox develops AI revenue agents designed to help large enterprises identify commercial opportunities, generate sales pipelines and automate customer-facing workflows.
Its platform supports tasks ranging from prospect research and lead qualification to personalized outreach, meeting scheduling, deal management and account expansion.
The agents operate within companies’ existing systems and leverage enterprise customer data to support sales execution.
Rather than simply generating recommendations or content, Rox aims to enable AI agents to take action across revenue workflows and deliver measurable commercial outcomes.
ARR Grew More Than 10x in Its First Year
Rox said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew more than tenfold in its first year in the market, as the platform expanded across enterprise customers in technology, energy, industrial and financial services sectors.
Its customer base includes companies such as Groq, Ramp and Puma Energy. Rox also reported net revenue retention exceeding 700% among enterprise customers, reflecting significant expansion in revenue from existing accounts.
The company is positioning its platform around measurable business impact, including pipeline generation, customer engagement and sales productivity.
Funding to Accelerate AI Research and Enterprise Expansion
Rox plans to use the new capital to advance AI research, develop custom models and strengthen its evaluation infrastructure for real-world revenue tasks.
The company also intends to expand its enterprise customer base across healthcare, industrial manufacturing, financial services, energy and technology.
Why AI Revenue Agents Are Attracting Investors
The funding highlights a broader shift in enterprise AI, from tools that generate content or assist employees to agents capable of executing complex workflows and connecting data with business actions.
Sales is emerging as a major application area because it involves extensive customer data, repetitive administrative tasks and multiple interconnected processes, from prospecting to account management.
However, the long-term opportunity for Rox will depend on its ability to demonstrate sustainable customer returns, scale enterprise deployments and compete with established customer relationship management platforms.
The investment underscores growing venture capital interest in AI agents that can deliver measurable operational and commercial outcomes, positioning autonomous enterprise workflows as a major frontier in AI adoption.
